issue.title: Cut the Full CI heavy-lane cost outliers: just test-cost (73 min) and coverage-contexts (38 min)
issue.description: Full CI takes ~1h43m against a two-hour schedule, leaving no headroom before ci_watch's heavy_max_age_hours freshness window starts holding the release shut. Two jobs dominate: just test-cost at 73 min for the same suite just test runs in 29, and coverage-contexts at 38 min. Deferred as R7 by plan 202608/release_gate_liveness.md section 9; proposed by the sase-um land agent from PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note 5 on phase bead sase-um.8.

task_type_fields.proposal:
Cut the two heavy-lane cost outliers so `Full CI` finishes well under its two-hour
schedule interval, instead of the ~1h43m it takes today.

Measured while planning epic sase-um (2026-08-26, per-job wall on one master `ci.yml`
run):

| Job                              | Wall   | Runs                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------- |
| `test (3.13)` (`just test-cost`)  | 73 min | same suite as `just test` |
| `coverage-contexts`               | 38 min | fast suite + per-test contexts |
| `test (3.12)` (`just test-cov`)   | 45 min |                          |
| `test (3.14)` (`just test`)       | 29 min |                          |

`just test-cost` runs 73 minutes against `just test`'s 29 for the *same* suite -- a 2.5x
multiplier paid entirely by the cost plugin. `coverage-contexts` is 38 minutes for a
baseline whose artifact is retained 14 days.

Concretely: attribute where `test-cost`'s 44-minute overhead goes and either bound it,
sample it, or move it to its own less frequent schedule; and decide whether
`coverage-contexts` needs to run on every two-hour heavy-lane tick or on a slower
cadence of its own, given the baseline it publishes is consumed by
`just refresh-contexts-baseline` and tolerates being hours old.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
This is heavy-lane budget, not gate budget: after epic sase-um these jobs run on a
schedule off the master push path, so they cost wall-clock on `Full CI` and org runner
minutes, but they do not sit between a commit and its gate result. The epic's own
acceptance criteria are about the fast gate's latency and the release opening, and none
of them move if `test-cost` gets cheaper. Plan `202608/release_gate_liveness.md` section
9 records R7 as explicitly deferred out of that epic and directs that it be filed as a
task bead.

It is worth doing separately because a heavy lane that takes 1h43m against a two-hour
schedule leaves almost no headroom: one slow run and the next scheduled tick either
overlaps (serialized by `full-ci` concurrency) or the newest green `Full CI` run ages
past `ci_watch`'s `heavy_max_age_hours` window and holds the release shut.
